lesson.title: "What's our total weight in each region?"
messages: Quick one before the 2pm: what's our total weight in each region?
lesson.body: Adding by hand works for 6 rows, not for 600. pandas does it in one line with `groupby`.

lesson.title: You are the groupby: sort each holding into its region pile

steps.text: Here's `df`: six holdings across three regions.
**Split.** pandas reads the `region` column and tags each row with its group.
Rows with the same region are gathered into piles. Nothing is added up yet.
**Apply + combine.** Pick the `weight` column, `sum` each pile, and you get one row per region.

lesson.title: Change it up and watch the result

region|sum.say: In plain English: it adds up the weights in each group, one result per region.

region|mean.say: In plain English: it averages the weights in each group, one result per region.

region|count.say: In plain English: it counts how many rows land in each group, one result per region.

region|max.say: In plain English: it finds the biggest weight in each group, one result per region.

sector|sum.say: In plain English: it adds up the weights in each group, one result per sector.

sector|mean.say: In plain English: it averages the weights in each group, one result per sector.

sector|count.say: In plain English: it counts how many rows land in each group, one result per sector.

sector|max.say: In plain English: it finds the biggest weight in each group, one result per sector.

questions.why: `mean` averages each group: Europe (5+4)/2 = 4.5, Asia (3+5)/2 = 4.0, EM (2+1)/2 = 1.5. The 9 / 8 / 3 answer is what `sum` would give.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of this line in order.
items: Split the rows into piles by region
Add up the weight inside each pile
Combine the totals into one small table, one row per region
questions.why: Split, apply, combine. Group the rows first, do the math on each group, then put the answers together.

options: It sorts the table by sector.
It adds up the portfolio weight for each sector, so you get one total per sector.
It removes duplicate sectors from the table.
It adds all the weights into one number.
questions.thanks: Ohh, one total per sector. That makes sense, thanks!
questions.why: groupby plus sum gives one total **per group**. Sorting or de-duping doesn't do any math, and one single number would just be `df['weight'].sum()`.
